definition: Discern means to make out or recognize something subtle or hard to notice through careful attention.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word discern. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know discern should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Standing on the dark porch, Leo could barely discern the outline of the mountains against the night sky.
Notice describes perception that simply happens to you, while discern suggests deliberate effort to pick out something subtle.
Discern is gentler than scrutinize, which means to examine something intensely and critically, inch by inch.

To perceive is the broad word for becoming aware of anything through the senses or the mind, however that happens. To discern adds effort and subtlety: you discern only what takes careful attention to make out, like a faint outline or a hidden pattern. All discerning is perceiving, but perceiving needs no work at all.

To detect is to discover the presence of something hidden or faint, and it is the natural word for instruments - a sensor detects a gas leak, a test detects a virus. To discern emphasizes the patient human attention that teases a subtle thing out. A machine detects in an instant; a trained eye discerns over long minutes.

To distinguish is to tell two things apart - to register the difference between them, like twins or two shades of blue. To discern is to make out one subtle thing at all. You distinguish a forgery from an original by comparing them; you discern the tiny flaws hiding inside a single canvas.

Discern means to make out or recognize something subtle or hard to notice through careful attention.
An art restorer examined the painting under a bright lamp for nearly an hour.
Slowly she began to discern tiny irregularities in the brushstrokes, details invisible to a casual viewer, that revealed the canvas was a forgery.
The restorer perceives something subtle only through careful, sustained attention, which is the core of discern: detecting what is not immediately obvious.
Discern suits careful, effortful perception of subtle things; when something is obvious, plain words like notice or tell sound more natural.
Also watch a classic confusable: discern (to perceive or detect) is unrelated to discreet (careful and tactful about what you say or do), despite the similar look and sound.

The dawn chorus at the refuge sounds, to most visitors, like a single wall of birdsong.
Okafor stands still in it for twenty minutes at a stretch, eyes closed, head tilted.
Somewhere inside the noise is the thin, two-note call of the marsh wren she has tracked all spring.
It takes her that long, most mornings, to discern the call at all; the wren sings faintly and rarely, and the chorus swallows it.
Students with sharp young ears still miss it, she says, because the skill is not hearing but attention: the patient work of making one faint thing come forward.
